GenKI stands for a system or model designed to enhance open-domain question answering. It is a novel framework that focuses on knowledge integration and controllable generation in large language models. GenKI aims to improve the performance of open-domain question answering (OpenQA) by integrating knowledge and generating more accurate and controllable responses.

The GenKI framework is proposed to address the limitations of existing models that rely on search engines to gather knowledge, which can be restrictive. GenKI has been evaluated on various benchmarks, including TriviaQA, MSMARCO, and CMRC, and has shown to consistently surpass baseline performances.

GenKI is also associated with a specific project or system, with its code available on GitHub at https://github.com/USTCStarTeam/GenKI. It is built on top of large language models, such as GLM-6B, and has been presented as a novel OpenQA framework that enhances the overall performance of question answering tasks.
